name: 1729 Prairie Avenue — the Pullman estate's stable and one-storey ranges (the district draft's massing, kept by T-1880; the stable refined to its pictures by T-3192)

grade.why: Pictured: a picture on the Images tab shows it.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 43.750, v -3.500 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation 179.611 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 1729 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1729 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).

footprint.note: The stable's south block as the 1911 sheet draws it (s20fp-1729-b1 p3), from its west wall (u -21.0) to its east wall (u -36.4), the canted south-east corner squared, and from the sheet's offset at v 1.5 to its 18th Street front (v 14.27), in the Pullman house draft's frame (u toward Prairie Avenue, v south). The draft's rectangle had stopped at u -32.25, the narrower north block's line; T-3192 carried it to the east wall, which Taylor's 18th Street photograph confirms (the hipped roof spans the sheet's block within about 0.5 m through its camera). The other parts are in draft_plan.

stories.note: '2' printed on the 1911 sheet over the east building (GARAGE); the ranges are one storey ('1B', '1').

construction.note: The register reads the map's colours as 'stone'.

parts.from: s20fp-1729-b1 p3 (main, stone): the east building's south block from its west wall to its east wall, as the 1911 sheet draws it with the canted south-east corner squared (T-3178), where the draft's rectangle 2 had stopped 4.2 m short of the east wall
s20fp-1729-b1 p3 (main, stone): the east building's narrower north block, from the sheet's offset at v 1.5 to its north wall (T-3178)

not on the 1911 sheet: the stable's 18th Street front carried on east of the sheet's east wall, as J. W. Taylor's 18th Street photograph shows it under a lower roof (T-3178); its depth is reconstructed
s20fp-1729-b1 p3 (main, stone), the draft's rectangle 3 (the 1B range north of the house's rear), stopped at the K01 house's north wall
s20fp-1729-b1 p4 (range, stone), the porte-cochere marked '1', stopped at the K01 house's 18th Street pavilion

draft_plan.note: The sheet's rectangles the K01 house does not carry, in the Pullman house draft's frame. The stable (T-3192): its south block r1 between the sheet's west and east walls, its narrower north block r4 at the sheet's offset, and r5, an east section the 1911 sheet does not draw: Taylor's 18th Street photograph shows the stable's two-storey front running on about 4 m past the hipped roof under a lower roof, with a third bay of sash, so r5 stands there at the photograph's length and the front's height; its 7.3 m depth is reconstructed (liberty L-pullman-stable-3192). The 1B range and the porte-cochere stay at one storey under flat roofs, as the sheet letters them. Roofs per piece other than the stable's are the draft rules' (reconstructed).

draft_elevation.note: The stable's elevation is T-3192's, read from its pictures; the rest is the draft rules' service elevation (T-1880). READ THROUGH TAYLOR'S 18TH STREET CAMERA (data/reference_views/pullman_house_1729_prairie_conservatory/taylor_16555_west_front.json, 23.8 px/m at the stable's front, about 10% scale uncertainty): the first-floor cornice 3.95 m over grade, from which the hipped roof springs at 53 degrees to a flat deck at 10.2 m inside iron cresting; the upper storey carried up through the roof's lower slope as one long wall with its own cornice at 6.0 m, a low attic band with two small square lights over the arcade; the arcade's three round arches (crowns about 3.0-3.2 m) between the west wall and the polygonal bay; the bay 4.8 m across, projecting 1.4 m, its cornice at 4.9 m and a round-headed light in each of its three faces (heads about 2.65 m); three bays of sash east of it on both storeys (ground sills 1.2 m, heads 3.2 m; upper sills 4.3 m); the deck's west edge 3.3 m in from the eave, read off the photograph's corner finial. FROM THE 1894 INLAND PLATE AND TAYLOR'S SOUTH-WEST VIEW, READ FOR FORM ONLY (their cameras are T-3193's): the arcade's broad open middle arch between two narrower lights, the lantern (an octagonal drum of lights under a dome and finial, placed toward the deck's west end, its size scaled from the south-west view), the stack at the front's east end rising about 1.3 m past the deck, and the square belvedere with cornice and balustrade over the range's parapet at the wing's east end (its top about 10.3 m through Taylor's camera at the range's face; its depth behind the parapet is reconstructed). RECONSTRUCTED, and kept at that tier for the field as a whole: the deck's other three insets, the lantern's and the stack's exact places, the north block's and the east section's roofs, the belvedere's depth, and the north, east and west faces' sash (the draft rules'). Liberty L-pullman-stable-3192 (and L-draft-prairie-16-18-east-2335 for what the draft rules still set).

function.note: The 1911 sheet's two-storey building at the lot's east end, lettered GARAGE (a 1911 use), with the one-and-a-half-storey part beside it, where the estate's stable stood (the Inland Architect's 1894 plate of the palm house and stable); the one-storey ranges are the sheet's 1B range north of the house's rear and the one-storey porte-cochere on 18th Street.

built.note: The marker: 'George M. Pullman Residence. Built 1870-1876'.

citations.citation: J. W. Taylor (Chicago), photographer. Pullman, George M., Residence [from the south-west, showing the palm house and stable]. Photograph, c. 1890-1910 (holder's view date). Art Institute of Chicago, Ryerson and Burnham Archives, Architecture Photograph Collection (Historic Architecture and Landscape Image Collection), no. 16554.
what_it_supplies: the stable's window count east of the bay (three bays, two storeys) and the stack at its east end
the lantern's form (octagonal drum with lights, a dome and a finial) and its place toward the deck's west end
what_it_does_not_supply: the arcade, which the bay and the planting hide from this side

citations.citation: J. W. Taylor (Chicago), photographer. Pullman, George M., Residence [west front, showing portion enclosing palm house and stable]. Photograph, c. 1890-1910 (holder's view date). Art Institute of Chicago, Ryerson and Burnham Archives, Architecture Photograph Collection (Historic Architecture and Landscape Image Collection), no. 16555.
what_it_supplies: the palm house's size and place along the range: about 7.6 m across its entablature, its centre about 12 m east of the house's east wall (19.8 px/m between the range's two ends)
the drum's columns, entablature, balustrade and dome, and their heights through its camera
the range's parapet height, its arched door and window, the terrace and its central flight of steps
what_it_does_not_supply: the rotunda's north half behind the range, the range's roof and its north side
the dome's covering (glass or metal) at this size

citations.citation: 'Lost Houses of Prairie Avenue: 1600-1700 Blocks', Prairie Avenue Historic District interpretive marker, Chicago; transcription on the Historical Marker Database (HMdb), marker 308722.

Pullman's theatre, organ and bowling alley and Beman's conservatory additions, in paraphrase

citations.citation: Inland Architect Press. Palm House and Stable of George M. Pullman, Chicago. S. S. Beman, Architect. Photographic plate in The Inland Architect and News Record, vol. 24, no. 1 (1894). Art Institute of Chicago, Ryerson and Burnham Archives, Archival Image Collection (Inland Architect plates).
what_it_supplies: the stable's forms: the arcade's three arches, the polygonal bay and its round-headed lights, the upper storey's wall and lights, the roof's west end springing from the first-floor cornice, the deck's cresting and the lantern
the belvedere's form: a square tower with a cornice and balustrade over the range's parapet

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 20.
what_it_supplies: The Illinois Central / Michigan Central right-of-way and, from the 16th Street row south about 60 m, the water's edge beside it, as of 1911
Footprints, lot lines, street widths (66 ft; 16th Street 50 ft), addresses, material by colour and story counts for Indiana Av. to the tracks, 16th to 18th Street, as of 1911
Its own printed Scale of Feet, which the georeference uses as its scale
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: The parts of the 1911 sheet's trace s20fp-1729-b1 that the Pullman house's K01 record (pullman_house_1729_prairie, T-1880) does not carry, kept where and as the district draft (T-2335) stood them so that nothing the sheet draws goes missing while the house moves onto K01: the stable and garage block at the lot's east end at two storeys, the 1B range north of the house's rear at one storey, and the porte-cochere on 18th Street at one storey. K01's wings stand on the main block's rear wall, and these do not (the conservatory, its own K13 record, stands between). Written by T-1880 on the draft builder from the draft's own rectangles, not by the draft rules (the rules' skip names it); every height, roof and opening is the draft rules' reconstruction (liberty L-draft-prairie-16-18-east-2335). T-1934 refines it; T-3192 refined the stable to J. W. Taylor's 18th Street photograph (AIC 16555) through the camera T-3165 solved on it, reading the stable's forms from the 1894 Inland Architect plate of the palm house and stable and Taylor's south-west view (AIC 16554), whose cameras are T-3193's (liberty L-pullman-stable-3192).
